failures.title: Mercedes-Benz OM603 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch - All variants, especially turbo
items.whatHappens: The timing chain and guides can stretch and wear over high mileage, leading to a distinct rattling noise on cold starts. If ignored, it can jump a tooth, causing valve-to-piston contact and catastrophic engine failure.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, a timing chain kit replacement is straightforward and cost-effective. If the engine has already suffered valve damage, a full reconditioned unit is the only viable path.

items.title: Injector Seal Weeping ("Black Death") - All variants
items.whatHappens: The copper washer seals at the base of the injectors degrade over time, allowing combustion gases to escape. This creates a black, crusty carbon buildup around the injector heads and can lead to difficult cold starts or rough idling.
items.repairVsReplace: This is a routine maintenance item, not a terminal failure. Replacing the seals and cleaning the head is inexpensive and should be done preventatively.

items.title: Head Gasket Failure - .960 turbocharged variants
items.whatHappens: The turbocharged OM603.960 variants generate significantly higher cylinder pressures and heat. Over time, the head gasket can fail, leading to coolant loss, overheating, and combustion gases entering the cooling system.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught before the cylinder head warps, a head gasket replacement is viable. If the head has warped or the block is damaged, a full reconditioned or rebuilt unit is required.

failures.goodYearsLine: The OM603 is widely regarded as one of Mercedes’ most robust inline-6 diesels, often outlasting the OM617 it succeeded in daily drivability. Units maintained with regular oil changes routinely exceed 300,000 miles without major internal issues .

variants.title: OM603 Sub-Codes Explained - Which One Is in Your Car?
variants.intro: INTRO: The OM603 family shares the same fundamental 3.0L inline-6 block and pre-chamber head design, but forced induction and tuning vary depending on the chassis. Identifying your exact sub-code ensures you order the correct injection pump, turbo, and ancillary components. - Fitted to: E-Class W124 (300D), S-Class W140 (300SDL), G-Class W463 (300GD) - Key technical difference: The base naturally aspirated variant, featuring a simpler ancillary layout without turbo plumbing and a mechanical injection pump calibrated for lower output. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; no unique widespread defects beyond standard high-mileage wear. - Interchange note: Not a straight swap with the turbo variants; the injection pump, exhaust manifold, and oil return lines differ significantly. - Fitted to: E-Class W124 (300TD), S-Class W140 (350SD, 350SD Turbo), G-Class W463 (350GD Turbo) - Key technical difference: Adds a turbocharger and intercooler to the 3.0L block, requiring a higher-capacity mechanical injection pump, revised piston cooling jets, and an upgraded cooling system to handle the additional heat. (Note: Later turbo revisions like .961, .962, and .963 share this core architecture). - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; turbocharger shaft wear and head gasket failure under boost are the primary additional wear items. - Interchange note: Can be swapped with the .910 block, but requires the complete turbo kit, different injection pump, and revised engine management linkages.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement OM603 Engine - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used OM603 engine makes sense only if it comes with verifiable service history and a recent timing chain replacement. Given the age of these vehicles, the primary risk is hidden corrosion or degraded rubber seals, so a compression test is mandatory before purchase.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned OM603 engine is the sweet spot for most buyers. A reputable rebuild will address the common failure points by fitting a new timing chain kit, updated injector seals, and a refreshed mechanical injection pump, giving the engine a fresh lease on life.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full OM603 engine rebuild is justified for high-mileage commercial G-Class applications or classic W140 restorations where originality and maximum longevity are required. An upgraded rebuild should include line-boring the block, new pistons/rings, and a balanced crankshaft.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting through our vetted network ensures your OM603 engine is installed by specialists familiar with classic Mercedes mechanical diesels, backed by a nationwide warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Because the OM603 is typically found in vehicles valued between £2,000 and £8,000 for standard examples (though classic low-mileage W140 and G-Class models can command much higher premiums), a full replacement can represent a significant portion of the car's worth. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing .

items.question: How much does a Mercedes OM603 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Mercedes OM603 engine typically costs between £1,800 and £2,800 for supply only . Fitted costs generally range from £2,700 to £4,000 depending on the specialist, while used units can be found from £600 but carry higher risk due to the engine's age. Compare OM603 engine replacement quotes today

items.question: What is the most common failure on the OM603 engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues are timing chain stretch and injector seal weeping, alongside head gasket failure on the turbocharged .960 variants. Timing chain rattle on cold starts is the primary warning sign of stretch, which can lead to catastrophic valve damage if ignored, whereas injector seal failure causes black carbon buildup around the injector heads but is a cheap and routine fix. Get quotes for a rebuilt OM603 with these issues resolved

items.question: Which Mercedes models use the OM603 engine?
items.answer: The OM603 was fitted to the W124 E-Class (300D, 300TD Turbo), the W140 S-Class (300SDL, 350SD, 350SD Turbo), and the W463 G-Class (300GD, 350GD, 350GD Turbo), serving as the definitive 6-cylinder diesel for these premium chassis. Check your registration to confirm your exact OM603 fitment

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned OM603 engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned OM603 is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the age of these vehicles. A proper rebuild will replace the timing chain, tensioner, and injector seals, eliminating the most common failure points, whereas used engines may appear cheaper upfront but often hide degraded rubber seals and stretched chains that will fail shortly after installation. Compare reconditioned OM603 engine prices from UK specialists

items.question: What is the difference between OM603.910 and OM603.960?
items.answer: The OM603.910 is the 3.0L naturally aspirated variant found across the W124, W140, and W463 range, while the OM603.960 is the turbocharged version. The .960 requires a higher-capacity mechanical injection pump, revised piston cooling jets, and an upgraded cooling system to handle the additional heat and cylinder pressures.
